description_intent: macOS treats the length of an update deferral as a configurable number an administrator sets, not a fixed built-in waiting period baked into the operating system - an organization can choose to hold back a released software update for some number of days before it installs. This control puts a ceiling on that configurable number itself: whatever number an organization sets, it may not exceed 30 days.
rationale_intent: A software update becomes a public disclosure of what needed fixing the moment it ships - the fix and the knowledge of the defect it closes arrive together, whether or not any given device has installed it yet. A deferral window exists so that compatibility testing doesn't have to be skipped, but an unbounded one erases the distinction between 'still testing' and 'never catching up' - both look identical in the moment, and only a ceiling on the deferral forces that difference to actually show up. Capping the number at 30 days keeps the trade-off an organization is allowed to make bounded: some room to test, but not so much that a defect already known to be fixed elsewhere sits open on this device indefinitely.
